ella.title: Dinner Is a Competition
ella.text:
Ella challenges you to dinner. It's a competition, naturally. Each of you orders, and whoever chooses the better meal wins.

She arrives early. By the time you sit down she has read the menu twice, questioned the waiter about the fish, and written something on her cuff.

She wins the first course. You win the second, by accident, and she tastes yours and is furious.

Then she puts her fork down. The candle flame steadies between you.

"I was across the street," she says. "I saw the truck."

Her hand is still on her glass, but her knuckles are white.

"You asked me how I got here, and I told you it wasn't on the agenda. I've told myself every day since I woke up that I would never speak of it." She looks at you. "I ran into the road, Takahashi. I didn't decide to. I've never done anything in my life without deciding. I'm speaking of it now because you're here, and I can."
ngpp: Halfway through studying the menu she frowns at the salt cellar, as if checking a scorecard that isn't there. She has the faint sense she has done this before. Then she squares her shoulders, shakes it off, and signals the waiter.

"Odd," she says over her wine glass, brow knitted. "I knew which entree you'd pass on before you opened your mouth, Takahashi." She puts the glass down. "I also knew the waiter would get the fish wrong. Lucky guesses. I don't have those."

"This table," she says quietly, knuckles pale on the stem. "The cracked brass candleholder. Rain on the window. The truck, in my sleep. Don't look at me like that. I'm not confused, Sam. We have had this dinner before, and I've known it since we sat down."

choices.label: Reach across the table
choices.res: You reach across the table and take her hand. She lets you and doesn't comment, though her pulse beats hard against your thumb. She looks at the candle for a long time. When she speaks, there's a ghost of her usual crispness in it. "That counts as a point to you," she says, and her fingers close around yours.

choices.label: Order dessert and change the subject gently
choices.res: You ask what the tart is like and flag down the waiter. She blinks once and follows the change like a professional, and her composure settles back into place. "The tart. Obviously." The candle steadies. Under the table her foot finds yours and stays there, and she eats dessert as though nothing has been said at all.

image.comp: sitting across a candlelit dinner table from him, fork set down, serious and vulnerable, hand on her wine glass
image.setting: private corner table in a lantern-lit restaurant

ella.title: Scoring Points
ella.text:
You open the washroom door, and Ella is in the tub.

Her hair is pinned up with a pencil. There's a thick book propped open on the soap dish. Her reading glasses have fogged, and she glares at you over the top of them through the steam.

"You didn't knock," she says. "That's a point to me."

She doesn't cover herself. You can see her work it out. The moral high ground is hers, and it's worth more than modesty. If she grabs for a towel, she concedes that something has happened.

So she turns a page. She does it with great calm.

She hasn't read a word of it. Her eyes aren't moving, and a flush is climbing slowly up from her collarbones. The water comes about as high as it needs to, and no higher.

"Well?" she says, without looking up. "Are you going to stand in the doorway letting the heat out, or are you going to contest it?"

1.text:
You open the washroom door, and Ella is in the tub with her hair pinned up on a pencil and her glasses fogged on her nose.

She doesn't snap at you. The corner of her mouth twitches upward.

"You didn't knock, Takahashi. That's a point to me." She tilts her chin back, and water runs down her throat and over her collarbone. She watches to see whether your eyes follow it, and they do. "If you'd like to appeal, you'll have to come closer. I don't hear cases from the doorway."

choices.label: Kneel beside the tub and earn your point back
choices.res: You kneel on the wet boards beside the tub. Steam clings to both of you. "Acceptable opening argument," she says, but her voice has gone low. Your hand finds the back of her neck and her eyes close. She leans toward you, water running off her shoulder, and her glasses fog completely. She doesn't take them off.

choices.label: Concede the point and shut the door
choices.res: You concede and shut the door, and she calls through it, "Smart." You stand in the hallway for a moment with your pulse going. Five minutes later there's a cup of tea outside your door. The tag on it says DRAW, in her small square capitals, and the tea is the way you like it.

image.comp: in the bath, hair pinned up with a pencil, fogged glasses, chin tilted back, water running down her throat, amused smirk

3.text:
You open the washroom door. Ella is pulling the pencil out of her hair, and it falls loose around her bare shoulders.

She sets her book down flat on the stool. Then she leans back against the rim with her arms along it. Her tits are out of the water and her long legs are parted under it, and she lets you look.

"You're late, Sam." Her voice has dropped. "I'm three points ahead, and I'm bored, and I've been touching myself for ten minutes thinking about how you'd lose. Get in here and settle the tie-breaker."

choices.label: Lock the door and climb into the bath with her
choices.res: You turn the key in the lock. She watches you do it, leaning back on her arms. "About time," she says, and when you pull your shirt over your head she doesn't pretend to look away. You step toward the tub and she catches your wrists before you sit, her hands wet and hot and sure of themselves.

choices.label: Wash her hair first and tease her about the score
choices.res: You pick up the soap and kneel behind her instead. Her hair comes down under your hands. She leans back against your palms and sighs, long and defeated, and you lean down to tell her exactly how the score stands. She laughs, low in her throat. "Pure bribery," she says. "Ten points. Keep going."

image.comp: leaning back against the rim with arms along it, hair loose over bare shoulders, breasts above the water, long legs parted under it, heated half-lidded gaze

choices.label: Concede the point and leave
choices.res: You concede the point. "Good," she says, and writes it in the margin of her book with the pencil from her hair. You pull the door shut on the steam. An hour later there's a cup of tea outside your door, still hot. There's a slip of paper under it with the word DRAW, underlined twice.

choices.label: "Then I'll earn it back."
choices.res: "Oh?" The corner of her mouth moves. "Name your terms." You do, and she counters, and you negotiate through the steam for far longer than the situation warrants. She makes you amend two clauses. Neither of you seems eager to finish, and when you finally leave she is smiling at her book and hasn't turned a page.

else.res: "Out," she says, with great dignity, and points the pencil at the door. "The point stands. Also, you're letting the heat out." You go. Through the wood you hear a page turn, quickly, and then a sound that might be her laughing at you or at herself. You can't tell which.

choices.label: Compliment her and mean it
choices.res: You tell her the water suits her, and that you mean it. She goes very still. A delicate pink climbs her throat to her ears. "That wasn't in my scoring system," she says, and for once she has no rebuttal. She looks at her book, then at you, then at the water, and doesn't say anything else for a while.

image.comp: in a bath, hair pinned up, a book propped beside her, fixing the doorway with a cool unimpressed glare

ella.title: The Leaderboard
ella.text:
Ella has reorganized the house chores into a tournament.

There's a chalkboard in the kitchen now, with a leaderboard on it. There are points for linens, for bar stock, and for punctuality. There are small prizes. There's an appeals process, and it has a very strict deadline.

Morale has tripled. The maids are racing each other on the stairs. The cook has started saluting her.

She has not told anyone that she's also keeping a score of her own.

You find out when her notebook falls out of her apron pocket. It lands open in the flour dust on the kitchen floor.

One column is headed "Observations". It's about you, and it runs for pages. It has dates in it. The entries start as marks out of ten for decisions you've made about the house. Further down they stop being about the house.

Ella is standing absolutely still, with a tray in her hands. She's looking at the notebook on the floor, and she has gone a color you've never seen on her.

choices.label: Stay with her
choices.res: You stay, pick up the notebook, and read the column aloud, politely, because she has frozen. There are seventeen entries, and several are about your handwriting. She says nothing at all. She doesn't take the tray away from her chest, and she doesn't leave. When you finish she is still standing there, and her ears are red.

choices.label: Pull her into the pantry for an off-the-record review
choices.res: You take her by the wrist and walk her into the pantry. Flour dusts the front of her apron as you bolt the door. Her brisk composure breaks at once. She says something about an off-the-record review in a voice that shakes, and then you have her back against the shelves and her hands are in your shirt.

choices.label: Hand it back unread
choices.res: You close the notebook without reading a line and hand it back. She takes it with great dignity and tucks it into her apron. Her hands are not quite steady. "You are," she says, crisply, "unbelievably annoying." It sounds, for once, like a compliment. She puts the tray down, and picks it up again, and goes.

image.comp: holding a leaderboard chalkboard, caught as a small notebook falls out of her apron, mortified and composed at once
image.setting: busy inn kitchen with staff cheering in the background

ella.title: The Offer
ella.text:
A merchant house in the capital has written to Ella. They've seen what she did with your accounts. They're offering her chief of accounts, with a salary and a title and a corner office that will have her name lettered on the door.

On paper it's everything she has ever wanted. It ranks her first at something.

She brings the letter to the ledger room, lays it on the desk in front of you, and says nothing. She puts her hands flat on the wood on either side of it.

Then she watches your face.

You know this look. She used to stand at the results board with it, already certain of her own mark, waiting to see yours.

She has decided what she wants you to say. She isn't going to tell you. If she has to ask you for it, it won't count.
ngpp: She sets the heavy parchment down, and her thumb lingers on the wax crest. She frowns at it. The seal is nothing special, and she can't say why it bothers her. She smooths the letter flat and the frown stays on her face.

"Funny," she says tightly. "Last night I dreamed I tore a letter with this exact seal down the spine. I don't dream, Takahashi. I've never kept one." She looks at the crest again. "I'd like to know why my hands are already deciding."

"I already know how this turns out, don't I?" she says over the parchment, eyes bright. "Corner office on paper, and my feet won't leave this plank floor. I've done this. I picked something. I want you to tell me whether I picked right."

choices.label: "Take it. You'd be the best they've ever had."
choices.res: "Take it. You'd be the best they've ever had." She nods once. "I hate how much I wanted you to say that," she mutters, and smooths the letter with the side of her hand. Her mouth is thin. She doesn't answer the merchants for a week, and she checks your face every time you pass her in the hall.

choices.label: "Stay. Beat me here."
choices.res: "Stay. Beat me here." "That's cheating," she says, but her eyes are bright. She turns the offer down the next morning, in writing, with a flourish of the pen that nearly tears the page. She brings you the copy before she posts it. At the bottom she has underlined her own name twice.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: You say nothing. She folds the letter and tucks it away, and she gives you a look you can't read. It isn't anger. It's something closer to a mark. She leaves the room without slamming the door. The house is colder for days. The leaderboard stays unchalked, and nobody in the kitchen will say why.

image.comp: sitting at a desk with a sealed offer letter in front of her, watching him with a level searching gaze
image.setting: ledger room, lamplight, neat stacks of paper

ella.title: Rematch
ella.text:
Ella sets up a chessboard in the courtyard at dusk. She's brought a brass clock. She's lettered a scoreboard by hand, and it says SAM vs. ELLA, GAME 1 OF 1.

"One game," she says. "No rematches. I want a result."

You play for two hours without speaking. The lanterns come on one by one around you. The clock ticks. She plays as she always did, three moves ahead and merciless. You play as you always did, which is to say you blunder into something that works.

At the end she has you cornered. It's mate in one, and you can both see it.

She looks at the board.

She looks at you.

Her hand goes out over her queen. It stays there. The clock is still running on her side, and she lets it.

She doesn't make the move. You have known her for six years, and you've never once seen her fail to take a win.

choices.label: Offer a draw
choices.res: You offer a draw. "Accepted," she says, much too quickly, and tips her own king over with one finger. "As a purely tactical choice." The clock is still ticking on her side. She leans across and stops it with her palm, and then she doesn't take her hand back, and you look at the lanterns instead of at her.

choices.label: Sweep the pieces aside and raise the stakes upstairs
choices.res: You sweep the pieces off the board with your forearm and tip the brass clock onto the flagstones. It rings once. She watches it roll. Her breath catches, and her cheeks go dark. You take her hand and lead her toward the stairs, and she follows without a single remark about the rules, which is how you know.

choices.label: Tell her to take the win
choices.res: "Take the win," you say. She stares at you, and then she takes it. She sweeps your king off the board and cheers, a bright unguarded whoop that makes the lantern boy jump. Then she is mortified, and then she buys you dinner out of sheer guilt and pays for the good wine, and refuses to be thanked.

image.comp: leaning over a chessboard, one hand hovering above a piece, looking up at him instead of the game
image.setting: lantern-lit courtyard table at dusk, chessboard between them

ella.title: First Place
ella.text:
Ella stops you on the stairs. She has a pencil in her hair and a ledger under her arm, and her chin is lifted for a fight.

"I have something to report, and I'd like you not to interrupt."

She sets the ledger down on the step.

"I came second to you for six years. I told everyone I hated it. I kept every list in a drawer and I looked at them more than was reasonable. I never minded. You were the only one worth losing to. Don't tell anyone."

She takes the pencil out of her hair, and it falls down around her shoulders.

"I ran into a road for you, and I didn't know why. I know now. I'm not competing any more, Sam. I've looked at the board, and I would like to be on your side of it."

She kisses you. It's decisive, as if it were the winning move, and you suppose it is.
ngpp: As her fingers pull the pencil loose, she blinks at the shadows on the landing. Her pulse is steady and strangely sure. She has the faint feeling this staircase ended here before. She doesn't know why, and she presses her mouth to yours.

"Weird," she says against your mouth, and pulls back half an inch. "My body already knew the stairs ended here. I didn't tell it. I never even rehearsed this part." She frowns, puzzled and unwilling to stop. "Don't mention it. I'll mark it as unexplained."

"Different life, same second place," she says into your collar, and clings to you. "I know it, Sam. Never mind the goddess and her resets. I kept every list. Put me in your column for good this time, because I'm not going to ask twice."
ella.goLead: You catch her by the waist on the landing and draw her through your bedroom door. The ledger and the pencil get left on the stairs. She has hold of your collar with both hands, like something she's won.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Ella nods briskly, as if filing it. "I can wait," she says. She picks up the ledger from the step and tucks it under her arm. Her chin is still lifted, though a little less. "But I'm tracking the delay, Sam. Don't make it too long. I don't lose on technicalities." She goes up the stairs, and she doesn't look back.
